deletion.accountDeletion: Kept iOS/Mac Settings → Delete account only

source.note: Every catalog input matches this commit; deployed discovery is verified separately.

tools.name: kept_get_today
tools.title: Get the day's snapshot
tools.description: Read the user's day at a glance for a date: events, habits with done state, the day's plan, sleep and mood. The one-call context block for grounding any day-specific answer.

tools.name: kept_list_tasks
tools.title: List open tasks
tools.description: List the user's open (not done) tasks, optionally filtered to one life area. Returns up to 50, soonest-due first.

area.description: A life-area label to filter by, or omit for all

tools.name: kept_list_asks
tools.title: List this app's asks
tools.description: List the asks this connected app made, including open, answered, sent-back, and withdrawn state plus any sent-back reason.

tools.name: kept_search_notes
tools.title: Search notes
tools.description: Full-text search the user's notes. Use to answer 'what did I write about…' and to ground answers in the user's own words. For meaning-shaped queries ('the pricing decision'), prefer kept_search_notes_semantic.

tools.name: kept_read_note
tools.title: Read a note
tools.description: Read one of the user's notes in full by id, including tasks linked to it (find the note first with kept_search_notes).

tools.name: kept_list_goals
tools.title: List goals
tools.description: List the user's active life goals. grounded_progress is their declared fraction or null; progress and metric_source retain the stored value and its source, not proof of measured achievement.

tools.name: kept_get_goal
tools.title: Get a goal
tools.description: Read one life goal by id, with its linked habits. grounded_progress is its declared fraction or null; a stored progress number with another metric_source is not a declaration or proof of achievement.

tools.name: kept_list_habits
tools.title: List habits
tools.description: List the user's active habits with their cue, target and minimum actions, cadence, recovery and review design, provenance, and calendar placement.

tools.name: kept_list_habit_groups
tools.title: List habit groups
tools.description: List the user's habit groups. Defaults to active groups; pass include_archived to include archived ones. Groups are optional labels distinct from part of day.

include_archived.description: When true, include archived groups. Default is active groups only.

tools.name: kept_list_areas
tools.title: List life areas
tools.description: List the user's declared life areas (key + label), so a caller can route new items to the right area.

tools.name: kept_list_calendars
tools.title: List calendars
tools.description: List the user's connected, writable calendars (id, name, purpose) so an event can be routed to the most relevant one.

tools.name: kept_check_calendar
tools.title: Check the calendar
tools.description: Read the user's events in a date range — to avoid conflicts before scheduling, or to find an event id before editing.

tools.name: kept_search_events
tools.title: Search events by name
tools.description: Find a calendar event by NAME (fuzzy — handles typos and partial titles). Use to answer 'when is X' or to find an event id when you only know its name, instead of guessing a date and scanning with kept_check_calendar. Returns the best matches with their date and time; an empty result means it isn't on the synced calendar (say so rather than inventing a date).

query.description: The event name or a fragment of it

tools.name: kept_recall
tools.title: Recall from memory
tools.description: Recall what Kept remembers about the user, semantically. Hybrid retrieval (meaning + keyword + recency + salience) over their long-term memory. Use for 'what does Kept know about my training / my routines / my coach'.

query.description: What to recall about the user

tools.name: kept_whoami
tools.title: Who am I
tools.description: Read the user's basic context: display name, timezone, and declared life areas. Resolve relative dates against this timezone. Minimal — no email or sensitive profile data.

tools.name: kept_search_docs
tools.title: Search Kept documentation
tools.description: Search Kept's verified product documentation for grounded answers about features, setup, privacy, billing, Apple apps, MCP, and Kept Workplace.

tools.name: kept_route
tools.title: Route a capture (no write)
tools.description: Classify a free-form line into the right kind (task, event, or note) with the user's full context — areas, priority, dates — and return the structured decision WITHOUT writing anything. Use when you want Kept's categorization but will decide yourself.

tools.name: kept_capture
tools.title: Capture and file
tools.description: Capture a quick line and let Kept file it as the right task, event, or note in the user's system — threaded to the right life area, and committed. The hero: 'log this to Kept'. Set dry_run to preview the routing without writing.

text.description: The line to capture, e.g. 'call the plumber Tuesday'

dry_run.description: Preview the routing decision without writing

tools.name: kept_create_task
tools.title: Create a task
tools.description: Create a task (something the user must do, with no fixed meeting time). Threads it to the matching life-area goal automatically. Use when you already know it's a task.

tools.name: kept_complete_task
tools.title: Complete a task
tools.description: Mark one of the user's tasks done by id (find it first with kept_list_tasks). Leaves a visible receipt on the task, since the person isn't watching this happen.

tools.name: kept_assign_task
tools.title: Assign this app's task
tools.description: Hand back or take on a task this exact connection created. Tasks created by the person or another connection cannot be reassigned here.

tools.name: kept_update_ask
tools.title: Update this app's ask
tools.description: Revise once or withdraw an ask this connected app made. The asking connection is derived from the token, never an argument.

tools.name: kept_log_note
tools.title: Log a note
tools.description: Save a note (a thought, idea, or reference) with an optional title and life-area folder. The fast-path for when you already know it's a note.

tools.name: kept_create_event
tools.title: Create an event
tools.description: Create a calendar event (something at a date/time/place). Writes to Kept and, optionally, a chosen connected calendar. Generate one UUID idempotency_key for the intended event, persist it, and reuse it unchanged for every transport retry.

idempotency_key.description: Caller-persisted UUID for this intended event. Reuse the same value after a timeout or lost response; a new value means a new event.

tools.name: kept_complete_habit
tools.title: Complete a habit
tools.description: Log one of the user's habits as done for a date (find the id with kept_list_habits).

tools.name: kept_create_goal
tools.title: Create a goal
tools.description: Create a life goal (title, optional north star, why, and life-area domain). For a full plan with habits and check-ins, the user opens the Goal Coach in-app.

tools.name: kept_remember
tools.title: Remember a fact
tools.description: Save a durable fact about the user to Kept's long-term memory (e.g. 'evenings are my weak point'). Kept embeds it for future recall.

tools.name: kept_forget
tools.title: Forget a memory
tools.description: Forget a memory by id (find it with kept_recall). This is a reversible soft-archive, not a hard delete — the memory can be restored.

tools.name: kept_update_task
tools.title: Update a task
tools.description: Edit one of the user's tasks: title, priority, due date, area, description, why, or labels. Find the id with kept_list_tasks. Pass only the fields you're changing; pass null for due/area to clear them.

tools.name: kept_reopen_task
tools.title: Reopen a task
tools.description: Reopen a completed task (mark it not done). Find the id with kept_list_tasks.

tools.name: kept_update_note
tools.title: Update a note
tools.description: Edit one of the user's notes: title, body, tags, or life-area folder. Find the id with kept_search_notes. Pass only the fields you're changing.

tools.name: kept_update_event
tools.title: Update an event
tools.description: Edit one of the user's calendar events: title, date, start/end, location, description, or area. Google-synced events update in Google too. Find the id with kept_check_calendar. Pass start as null for all-day.

tools.name: kept_update_goal
tools.title: Update a goal
tools.description: Adjust an existing life goal (title, north star, why, target value/date). Find the id with kept_list_goals.

tools.name: kept_set_goal_progress
tools.title: Set goal progress
tools.description: Record explicitly stated goal progress (0..1) as declared. This replaces its previous progress attribution; it does not measure achievement, complete tasks, or archive the goal. Find the id with kept_list_goals.

tools.name: kept_archive_goal
tools.title: Archive a goal
tools.description: Archive a life goal so it leaves the active list. Reversible (restorable in-app). Prefer this over deleting. Find the id with kept_list_goals.

tools.name: kept_create_habit
tools.title: Create a habit
tools.description: Create exactly ONE approved habit. Use kept_list_habits first and update a matching habit instead of duplicating it. New callers should include a stable idempotency key plus the cue, target, worst-day minimum, recovery, and review design; the legacy title/category shape remains supported.

idempotency_key.description: Caller-persisted UUID reused unchanged for transport retries.

scheduledTime.description: Local time of day (24h HH:mm) to place this habit on the calendar. Omit for a sensible default by category.

showOnCalendar.description: Whether the habit appears on the day calendar (default true).

tools.name: kept_update_habit
tools.title: Update a habit
tools.description: Adapt an existing habit's complete behavioral design. Use kept_list_habits first, pass only fields that should change, and prefer this over creating a duplicate for the same intention.

tools.name: kept_create_habit_group
tools.title: Create a habit group
tools.description: Create a habit group, or return the existing active group when this owner already has the same normalized name. Use kept_list_habit_groups first. Archiving is reversible; there is no delete.

tools.name: kept_update_habit_group
tools.title: Update a habit group
tools.description: Rename, archive, or unarchive one habit group. Pass a name and/or archived change; an empty patch is refused. Archiving does not unassign habits. Unique active names are per owner.

tools.name: kept_reorder_habit_groups
tools.title: Reorder habit groups
tools.description: Reorder active habit groups. ids must be a permutation of the current active catalog. Positions are written one at a time and are not an atomic reorder.

tools.name: kept_archive_habit
tools.title: Archive a habit
tools.description: Archive a habit so it no longer shows in the daily protocol. Reversible (its history is kept). Prefer over deleting. Find the id with kept_list_habits.

tools.name: kept_uncomplete_habit
tools.title: Uncomplete a habit
tools.description: Unmark a habit for a date (logged done by mistake). Find the id with kept_list_habits.

tools.name: kept_get_now
tools.title: What should I do now
tools.description: What the user should do right now — Kept's 'Now' brief with the engine's reasoning. Returns the latest brief; when missing/stale (or regenerate=true) it generates a fresh one via the LLM and caches it (a 45s burst guard avoids redundant generation). On a brand-new or fully-cleared account it skips the LLM and returns a friendly empty state instead.

tools.name: kept_prioritize_day
tools.title: Prioritize the day
tools.description: Kept's prioritized plan for a day — a Do-first list and Deep-work blocks chosen from the user's open tasks, each with a reason. Generates and caches the plan via the LLM; does NOT change the user's tasks (only the derived daily_plans row).

date.description: Defaults to today in the user's timezone

tools.name: kept_get_briefing
tools.title: Get the briefing
tools.description: The composed morning briefing for a date (from the Nightly Engine). Reads the latest if no date is given.

tools.name: kept_export_tasks
tools.title: Export tasks
tools.description: Export the user's tasks as JSON or Markdown, filterable by area / done state / due-before, capped and cursor-paginated. The 'export my todos' ask.

cursor.description: Row offset for the next page

tools.name: kept_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: List the user's calendar events in a date range, paginated. Returns safe fields only (no attendee emails, external ids, or sync metadata).

tools.name: kept_list_memories
tools.title: List memories
tools.description: List the user's salient long-term memories (most weighted first). For semantic recall on a topic, use kept_recall instead.

tools.name: kept_append_daily_note
tools.title: Append to daily note
tools.description: Append a line to today's daily note (get-or-create on the user's logical day). The 'jot this in today's note' fast-path.

tools.name: kept_search
tools.title: Search Kept
tools.description: Search across the user's notes (full-text) and open tasks (title match) at once — 'find anything in my Kept'. For meaning-shaped note queries ('the pricing decision'), prefer kept_search_notes_semantic.

tools.name: kept_search_notes_semantic
tools.title: Search notes by meaning
tools.description: Search the user's notes BY MEANING (semantic + keyword). Prefer this over kept_search_notes: it finds 'the pricing decision' even when the note said 'per-seat ceiling'. Returns the matching blocks in the user's own words.

query.description: What to find, in plain language

context.description: Restrict to the work or personal side

tools.name: kept_notes_about
tools.title: Thread / dossier
tools.description: Assemble everything the user ever noted about a person, project, goal, or topic — the auto-built thread/dossier, time-ordered. Use for 'what's the latest on Aisha' or 'everything about the Acme renewal'. The user never filed this; it gathered itself.

tools.name: kept_related_notes
tools.title: Related notes
tools.description: Given a note id, surface the few past notes most related to it (they share a person/project/topic). The scoped 'related' view, never a whole-vault graph.

tools.name: kept_decisions_about
tools.title: Decisions about
tools.description: Recall the DECISIONS the user recorded about a project, topic, or person — newest first, with the verbatim rationale. Use for 'why did we go with X' / 'why didn't we pick A'; keyword search can't find these (the note said 'relational shape', not 'Mongo').

name.description: The project/topic/person the decision was about

tools.name: kept_list_threads
tools.title: List threads
tools.description: List the user's auto-built note threads (entities): People, Projects, Goals, Decisions, and more, salience-ranked. Discover which entities exist before drilling in with kept_notes_about or kept_decisions_about.

kind.description: Restrict to one lens, e.g. person or project

tools.name: kept_note_chips
tools.title: Note chips
tools.description: Read a note's chips — the entities the Structurer linked to it, with confidence and auto/manual source. The 'what does Kept think this note is about' view.

tools.name: kept_list_note_templates
tools.title: List note templates
tools.description: List the user's note-template library: the curated seed templates plus their own promoted ones (name, shape, triggers, category — not the full skeletons).

tools.name: kept_list_note_folders
tools.title: List note folders
tools.description: List the user's note folders (id + name) for filing notes.

tools.name: kept_move_note_to_folder
tools.title: Move note to folder
tools.description: File one of the user's notes into one of their folders. Find the folder id with kept_list_note_folders and the note id with kept_search_notes.

tools.name: kept_link_note_to_task
tools.title: Link note to task
tools.description: Attach one of the user's notes to one of their tasks, so the note shows as reference on the task.

tools.name: kept_read_daily_note
tools.title: Read the daily note
tools.description: Read the user's daily note for a date (today by default, in their timezone). Read-only: returns exists=false if the day has no note yet — use kept_append_daily_note to start one.

date.description: The daily note's local date; defaults to today

tools.name: kept_note_blocks_read
tools.title: Read note blocks
tools.description: Read one of the user's notes as blocks — every paragraph, heading, checkbox, and list item with its own id, type, and nesting. Call this before kept_note_blocks_edit, which addresses blocks by these ids. Long notes come back a page at a time: pass the next_cursor you were given, or block_id to read one section and what is under it.

tools.name: kept_note_blocks_edit
tools.title: Edit note blocks
tools.description: Change part of one of the user's notes, leaving every other block exactly as they wrote it, ids included. Operations: insert_after, insert_before, replace, delete, and move, applied in order as one atomic edit — if any one of them cannot be placed, none of them are and nothing is written. Read the note with kept_note_blocks_read first and use the ids it gave you; never guess one. Prefer this over kept_update_note for anything short of a rewrite the person actually asked for.

tools.name: kept_list_subtasks
tools.title: List subtasks
tools.description: List the checklist items (subtasks) on one of the user's tasks. Find the task id with kept_list_tasks.

tools.name: kept_add_subtask
tools.title: Add a subtask
tools.description: Add a checklist item (subtask) to one of the user's tasks. Find the task id with kept_list_tasks.

tools.name: kept_set_subtask_done
tools.title: Set subtask done
tools.description: Check or uncheck a subtask. Find the id with kept_list_subtasks.

tools.name: kept_list_task_comments
tools.title: List task comments
tools.description: Read the comments on one of the user's tasks. Find the task id with kept_list_tasks.

tools.name: kept_add_task_comment
tools.title: Add a task comment
tools.description: Add a comment to one of the user's tasks (a status update, context, a note-to-self). Attributed to Kept. Find the task id with kept_list_tasks.

tools.name: kept_event_details
tools.title: Event details
tools.description: Read one event in full: who's invited, their replies, the organizer, the user's own RSVP, and whether it's shareable (on a connected Google calendar). Use before inviting or replying. Find the id with kept_check_calendar.

tools.name: kept_invite_to_event
tools.title: Invite to event
tools.description: Invite people to one of the user's events. Stages a Google invite the user confirms in Kept before anyone is emailed. Only works on events on a connected Google calendar (check kept_event_details · shareable). Never guess ids.

tools.name: kept_rsvp_event
tools.title: RSVP to event
tools.description: Reply to an event the user was invited to (accept, maybe, or decline). Stages the RSVP for the user to confirm in Kept, since it notifies the organizer. Works on events from a connected Google calendar. Find the id with kept_check_calendar.

tools.name: kept_move_event_to_calendar
tools.title: Move event to calendar
tools.description: Move one of the user's events to a different calendar of their own (e.g. Personal to Work). Immediate; emails no one. Find the target id with kept_list_calendars and the event id with kept_check_calendar.

tools.name: kept_list_focus_sessions
tools.title: List focus sessions
tools.description: List the user's focus sessions started in a date range (label, mode, minutes, completed), paginated. The 'how much deep work did I do this week' read.

cursor.description: Row offset for the next page

tools.name: kept_get_weight_trend
tools.title: Get the weight trend
tools.description: Read the user's weight readings over a date range, with Monday-based weekly averages already computed. Use this for questions about weight progress. Day-to-day swings can mislead, so prefer the weekly average. Ranges longer than 370 days are refused rather than silently truncated.

from.description: First day of the range, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD)

to.description: Last day of the range, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD)

tools.name: kept_get_sleep_range
tools.title: Get sleep over a range
tools.description: Read the user's nightly sleep over a date range, including time asleep, efficiency, awakenings, deep and REM sleep, Kept's score, and weekly averages. Use this for sleep patterns; kept_get_today gives only one night.

from.description: First day of the range, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD)

to.description: Last day of the range, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD)

tools.name: kept_get_mood_range
tools.title: Get mood over a range
tools.description: Read the mood the user logged over a date range, with weekly averages. Use this for mood patterns or to compare a felt claim with what they recorded.

from.description: First day of the range, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD)

to.description: Last day of the range, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD)

tools.name: kept_get_habit_history
tools.title: Get habit history
tools.description: Read the user's habit log over a date range with per-habit adherence already calculated. Pass a habit_id for one habit or omit it for all. Adherence uses days with log rows, so compare logged_days with the range before treating an unlogged day as a miss.

habit_id.description: One habit id from kept_list_habits, or omit for every habit

from.description: First day of the range, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD)

to.description: Last day of the range, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD)

tools.name: kept_get_metric_series
tools.title: Get a metric series
tools.description: Read the history of one metric the user tracks, including its target, direction, and weekly averages. Use its lower_snake_case key. An unknown key returns an explicit error rather than an empty series.

from.description: First day of the range, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD)

to.description: Last day of the range, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD)

tools.name: kept_search_tasks
tools.title: Search tasks
tools.description: Search the user's task titles by keyword, including completed tasks by default. Use when they name a specific task; kept_list_tasks only returns open tasks and cannot establish whether something was completed.

tools.name: kept_find_free_slots
tools.title: Find free slots
tools.description: Find openings of a given length in the user's working hours across a date range, combining connected-calendar free/busy with Kept events. Read-only: it books nothing. Check unanswered_calendars and unauthorized_accounts because a slot is only as certain as the calendars that answered.

from.description: First day of the range, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD)

to.description: Last day of the range, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD)

timezone.description: IANA timezone; defaults to the user's profile

tools.name: kept_get_event_guests
tools.title: Get event guest replies
tools.description: Read invitation responses for one event or across at most 31 days of meetings. Returns accepted, declined, tentative, and awaiting replies plus organizer status. Read-only: it uses the last calendar sync, sends no email, changes no RSVP, and never explains why someone did or did not answer.

event_id.description: One event id from kept_check_calendar, or omit to sweep a range

from.description: First day of a range sweep, inclusive

to.description: Last day of a range sweep, inclusive, at most 31 days

organized_by_them_only.description: For range sweeps, include only meetings the user organizes, default true

awaiting_only.description: For range sweeps, include only meetings awaiting at least one reply

tools.name: kept_create_job
tools.title: Create a job
tools.description: Create a Cloud Agents job for Kept to work on: an outcome (title + objective), not a to-do. Runs against your default agent unless you pass agent_id. Kept performs Class 0/1 actions (read-only or reversible, Kept-owned) automatically; anything higher-risk pauses for your approval, never performed by this tool itself. Find the job's progress with kept_get_job. Sensitive-context grants are not settable over MCP; a job created here starts with none.

objective.description: The outcome the job should reach, in your own words

agent_id.description: An existing agent id you own; omit to use your default agent

due_date.description: ISO 8601 datetime the job is due

tools.name: kept_get_job
tools.title: Get a job
tools.description: Read one Cloud Agents job's current state: title, objective, assigned agent, lifecycle status, and its most recent run's status. Find the id with kept_list_jobs.

tools.name: kept_list_jobs
tools.title: List jobs
tools.description: List your Cloud Agents jobs, most recently created first, each paired with its latest run's status and pending-approval count.

tools.name: kept_get_run_events
tools.title: Get run events
tools.description: Read a job run's normalized event timeline in order: state changes, tool calls, artifacts. User-visible events only, never raw model reasoning or provider traces. Find the run id with kept_get_job or kept_list_jobs.

tools.name: kept_submit_approval
tools.title: Decide an approval
tools.description: Decide a pending Kept approval by id. Requires echoing the exact parameter_hash you read (from kept_get_run_events or the Kept app); a stale or wrong hash is refused, never re-hashed for you. Class 3 (high-consequence) approvals can only be approved inside the Kept app, where the type-back confirmation is real; over MCP you may only reject a Class 3 approval or leave it for the user. Class 2 approvals may be approved, edited and approved, or rejected.

parameter_hash.description: Must exactly match the approval's current parameter_hash
